findings.text: 55 chemotype(s); the largest holds 61 of 282 molecules -- a series of several scaffolds has no common frame, and an alignment will invent one
the common framework (framework of the largest chemotype) has 17 heavy atoms, about 65% of a typical molecule, and 22% of the set can be cut at it
the 17 shared framework atoms sit 0.0 A apart between molecules, over the best of their matches (67 of 282 carry them)
the aligned model is +0.190 in q2 against counts (95% interval +0.109 to +0.283) -- the frame does better than counts
the aligned model is -0.015 in q2 against invariant (95% interval -0.076 to +0.055) -- the frame gains nothing over invariant
the aligned model is +0.253 in q2 against topomer (95% interval -0.030 to +0.675) -- cutting the molecules and posing the pieces by rule does as well as the frame, on the molecules that can be cut
the aligned model is +0.342 in q2 against descriptors (95% interval +0.251 to +0.439) -- the geometry adds something

why: the frame gains nothing over invariant, which needs no alignment to curate and cannot be done wrongly
